title: Non-vanishing of the layered minors of the Fourier matrix of order $pq$
author: Maria Loukaki
work: Chebotarev's theorem for groups of order $pq$ and an uncertainty principle
difficulty_reason: Even with the paper's own algebraic-number-theory preliminaries supplied - the splitting of the rational prime p in Z[zeta_n] and the identification of the residue field Z[zeta_n]/(1-zeta_p) as the field with p^{phi(m)} elements together with the primitivity of the image of zeta_r there (Lemma 3 and Lemma 4 of the delivered unit), the Dedekind-domain divisibility remark (Remark 2) and Frenkel's multiplicity bound (Lemma 5) - the counted main theorem is not a qualification exercise. The counted proof has to turn the vanishing relation into a single polynomial r(x) with the minimal power of 1-zeta_p divided out, homogenise it into the two-variable polynomial g(x,y), split the index set J into the r layers J_r^k, assemble the |L| x |L| layered system T_t = sum_{k in L} omega_r^{ptk} S_k, reduce the entire system modulo the prime ideal (1-zeta_p) so that Zhang's finite-field Chebotarev theorem becomes applicable to the layered matrix R-bar, and then run a genuine induction on the number of non-empty layers: invert R-bar, use Frenkel's lemma to force the coefficients of the smallest layer S_{k_1} to be divisible by 1-zeta_p, delete that layer from the reduced system, observe that the surviving matrix D-bar is again a square submatrix of the finite-field Fourier matrix and therefore still invertible, and repeat until every coefficient z_j is divisible by 1-zeta_p, contradicting the choice of r(x). Recognising that the reduced system keeps the same Chebotarev type at every step, and that Zhang's hypotheses (primitivity of p in Z_r and p > Gamma_r) survive the peeling, is a research-level assembly well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in number theory.
